refnamediv.refpurpose: Configure additional binary formats for executables at boot

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: systemd-binfmt.service is an early boot service that registers additional binary formats for executables in the kernel.
See binfmt.d5 for information about the configuration of this service.

refsect1.title: BPF Handlers
refsect1.para: A binary format can also be matched and dispatched by a BPF handler, see bpf-backed handlers. Each BPF object name.bpf.o found in the directories below is registered as the handler name, together with a rule name of type B that hands binaries to it. These rules are registered after the rules from binfmt.d5, in the order of the file names.

Packages should install their objects into /usr/lib/systemd/binfmt/. An object in /etc/ overrides an object with the same file name in /run/ and /usr/lib/, and an object in /run/ overrides one in /usr/lib/. A symlink to /dev/null or an empty file masks the object of the same name, and neither the handler nor the rule is registered.

The object must contain exactly one struct_ops map, of type binfmt_misc_ops, and the name the map sets for the handler must match the file name. If a handler of that name is registered already, the rule is written for the registered one. The rule keeps the handler alive on its own, so nothing but the rule is left registered.
Registering BPF handlers requires libbpf and a kernel built with CONFIG_BINFMT_MISC_BPF (Linux 7.3 or newer).

listitem.para: If passed, instead of registering configured binary formats in the kernel, the reverse operation is executed: all currently registered binary formats are unregistered from the kernel.
